lit.\u0027\u003cp class=\"muted small\"\u003:
"

E° at 25 °C, 1 mol/L; water is evaluated at the pH of the solution. Textbook guide: real products depend on the concentration, the electrode and the voltage.

"

"

Click or drag on the graph to change the voltage. Below E° + η (light blue line) the current is zero; above it grows linearly (Ohm's law in the solution).

"

"

The slope of H₂ is twice that of O₂ (2 : 1 ratio). The greater the current, the greater the slope (Faraday).

"

"

Overpotentials and resistances are approximate didactic values so that the cell behaves like real ones: exact data depend on the electrode, the current density and the temperature.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp class=\"note\"\u003e* Por:
"

* By the E° criterion water would win, but the overpotential of O₂ changes the real result.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003e\u003cb\u003en = Q /:
"

n = Q / (z·F), with Q = I·t, F = 96,485 C/mol and z = 2 for H₂ (z = 4 for O₂ per mole).

As the voltage increases the current increases and, therefore, so does the gas production rate. Watch how n(H₂) and V(H₂) rise in the table.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAl superar E° + η (≈:
"

When E° + η is exceeded (≈ 1.7 V for platinum) electrolysis begins: electrons travel through the external circuit, the cathode reduces and the anode oxidizes.

Look at the half-reactions in the upper box: they depend on the medium (acidic, neutral or basic), but the overall reaction is always the same.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCada 4 e⁻ producen \u:
"

Every 4 e⁻ produce 2 H₂ at the cathode and 1 O₂ at the anode. At equal temperature and pressure, gas volumes are proportional to moles (Avogadro): V(H₂) : V(O₂) = 2 : 1.

Check it in the panel's tubes: the H₂ one fills twice as fast.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eDos electrodos inerte:
"

Two inert electrodes are immersed in water with an electrolyte. Pure water barely conducts electricity (≈10⁻⁷ mol/L of ions), which is why an acid, a base or a salt is added.

The power supply forces a reaction that does not occur on its own: the (−) pole is connected to the cathode (reduction) and the (+) pole to the anode (oxidation).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa energía mínima par:
"

The minimum energy to obtain one mole of H₂ is ΔH° = 285.8 kJ (thermoneutral voltage 1.48 V). With a cell at V volts, 2·F·V joules are spent per mole of H₂.

The energy efficiency ≈ 1.48 / V: the higher the applied voltage, the more energy is dissipated in overpotentials and solution resistance.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa reacción global 2:
"

The overall reaction 2 H₂O → 2 H₂ + O₂ is nonspontaneous (ΔG° = +237 kJ per mole of H₂O). Its standard potential is ΔE° = −1.23 V, so more than 1.23 V must be applied.

In practice, the overpotential (η) of the electrodes must also be overcome, so between 1.23 V and the real decomposition voltage no appreciable current flows yet.

"
